title: Quota-conscious tiered routing with progressive model degradation
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement a quota-aware routing policy that enforces soft guarantees for paid and enterprise customers while allowing controlled degradation for free-tier traffic. Goals: 1) prioritize requests by subscription tier and remaining quota, 2) minimize P99 latency regressions for paid/enterprise during peak load, 3) automatically fall back to cheaper or lower-capability model variants when higher-tier capacity or quota is exhausted, 4) provide observable signals and config knobs for ops and product to tune behavior. This ticket covers policy design, admission control primitives, runtime admission hooks, config schema, and integration with Console metrics and routing UI.
acceptance_criteria: Routing decisions honor per-tenant remaining quota and declared priority (free < paid < enterprise)
Under quota exhaustion, free-tier requests are degraded first by redirecting to cheaper model variants or queuing according to configured policy

Paid and enterprise requests receive soft guarantees: bounded retries to alternate region or instance before degradation; latency SLO for paid should not exceed baseline + 10% under controlled overload
Routing policy can be toggled via Console feature flag and supports canary rollout
Telemetry emitted for every routing decision: chosen tier, quota snapshot, model variant, fallbacks triggered, and latency impact
Automated integration tests and load sims validate behavior for three traffic mixes (free-heavy, balanced, enterprise-heavy)
implementation_notes: Admission control: implement per-tenant token-bucket with fast-path approval; fallback path consults policy engine
Policy engine: deterministic decision order - check region affinity -> check subscription tier -> check quota token bucket -> evaluate model variant availability
Model variants: annotate models with cost-class and capability tags (e.g., v1-high, v1-low-quant, v1-merged-emb) to enable downgrade chaining
Quota smoothing: use EWMA over 1m window to avoid thrashing when quota replenishes; expose smoothing factor in config
Backpressure: implement priority-aware queuing with aging to prevent starvation of free requests when queues are lightly loaded
Circuit-breaker: per-region and per-model breaker to short-circuit to fallback variant and record event for ops
Metrics: counters for routing decisions, histograms for latency per tier/variant, gauges for token-bucket fullness, and traces for request path
Console UX: expose per-tenant quota meters, current policy version, and ability to override policy for single tenants
Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout -> canary to 5% of traffic -> monitor error/latency/downgrade rates -> progressive ramp
Safety: fail closed to paid/enterprise (i.e., if policy engine errors, prefer conservative routing that preserves paid SLA)
test_plan: Unit tests for policy engine decision tree and token-bucket behavior
Integration tests: end-to-end routing path with mock runtime and model-variant registry
Load tests: three scenarios using perf-harness: free-heavy (80% free), balanced (33/33/33), enterprise-heavy (60% enterprise)
Chaos tests: simulate region outage and validate cross-region fallback honors tier priorities
SLO verification: measure P50/P95/P99 latency for paid/enterprise slices under 2x baseline load
Telemetry verification: assert routing events contain quota snapshot, model_variant_id, and fallback_reason tags
